fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. The text says Absalom, David's son, invited all the sons of the king. That means every brother, Amnon included. A sheepshearing party with every one of the king's sons on the list, and I think that's a lot of mules to park.

Right, because the servants are invited too. Absalom says, “Will the king and his servants please come with me?” He asks for the king and his servants, not the king alone. So the statement that he asks the king to leave them at home is false.

Yes, Amnon. Absalom says, “If not… please let my brother Amnon go with us.” Amnon is David's oldest son (2 Samuel 3:2), and the text has already told us about what he did to Tamar. Absalom is asking for that one by name.

A tent never comes up in the text. Absalom says, “Watch Amnon until his heart is merry with wine…” The wine is what they're told to watch for, and Absalom's order to strike is the signal to kill Amnon. It's a heavy part of the story, so we'll keep it straight.
That's right. The text says, “…each one fled on his mule.” All the other sons of the king got up and left. Mules were what they rode, and they used them to flee.

True. The text says, “Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground.” The report he heard was that Absalom had struck down all the sons of the king. I think this one hurts, and tearing his clothes shows how hard the news hits him.
That's what Jonadab says: “…Absalom has planned this since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.” That tells us when the planning began. Jonadab names that day as the starting point.

Right. Jonadab says, “Look, the sons of the king have arrived! It is just as your servant said.” The watchman sees men coming, and Jonadab says they're the king's sons. Then the text says the sons of the king came in, wailing loudly.
